ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Yul Brynner Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: New patient visit for six weeks of hoarseness, with a left upper lobe mass on same-day CT. Concerns: His voice has become weak and breathy, and he cannot sing or project on stage; He wants to get back to performing and to keep working for as long as he can; He wants people to know what smoking did to him. [S]

tr.td: Pembrolizumab 200 mg intravenous infusion over 30 minutes every 3 weeks

Triamcinolone acetonide 0.1% cream, thin layer to the rash twice daily for two weeks (not on the face or skin folds)
Apply a thin layer twice daily for up to two weeks

One tablet by mouth daily as needed for itching

tr.td: Flexible laryngoscopy by the ENT surgeon: left vocal fold immobile in the paramedian position with incomplete glottic closure; no laryngeal mass or mucosal lesion

CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis with contrast: 5.2 cm left upper lobe mass invading the mediastinal fat of the aortopulmonary window and abutting the aortic arch and left pulmonary artery; enlarged aortopulmonary window (2.4 cm) and subcarinal (1.8 cm) lymph nodes; a small lytic lesion in the T10 vertebral body; no adrenal or liver lesion

FDG PET-CT: avid left upper lobe mass (SUVmax 14) with mediastinal invasion; avid aortopulmonary window and subcarinal nodes (N2); no contralateral or supraclavicular nodes; avid lytic lesions at T10, the right ilium, and the left sixth rib, without fracture (M1c)
MRI of the brain with contrast: no metastases

Endobronchial ultrasound-guided needle aspiration of subcarinal (station 7) and left lower paratracheal (4L) nodes: adenocarcinoma, TTF-1 and napsin A positive; PD-L1 (22C3) tumor proportion score 70 percent; tissue sent for comprehensive next-generation sequencing (reported 12 days later: KRAS G12V and TP53 mutations; no EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF V600E, KRAS G12C, MET exon 14, RET, NTRK, HER2, or NRG1 alteration), with concordant plasma cell-free DNA testing
Outpatient palliative care visit: symptom assessment, coping, goals of care, and a plan for breathlessness and cough
Office injection medialization of the left vocal fold under laryngoscopic guidance by the ENT surgeon, to improve glottic closure and voice
Advance care planning conversation, about 30 minutes

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Thoracic oncology consultation for the tissue diagnosis, stage, biomarker plan, first-line therapy, the place of radiation and a bone-modifying agent, and monitoring

Staging and tissue diagnosis: FDG PET-CT, brain MRI with contrast, and endobronchial ultrasound-guided needle aspiration of the highest-stage node, with enough tissue for PD-L1 and comprehensive next-generation sequencing, and plasma cell-free DNA testing in parallel

First-line systemic therapy chosen by biomarkers once sequencing excludes an actionable alteration: pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for PD-L1 50 percent or more, with response CT every 6 to 12 weeks; switch to 400 mg every 6 weeks to fit the tour once stable

Immune-related adverse event monitoring: TSH and free T4, liver tests, creatinine, glucose, and blood count before each infusion; morning cortisol at baseline and for symptoms; written list of warning symptoms (diarrhea, cough or breathlessness, rash, yellowing, severe fatigue or headache) with a 24-hour oncology telephone line
Early integrated palliative care alongside cancer treatment, starting within eight weeks of diagnosis, with symptom (ESAS) and distress screening at each visit and advance care planning

If bone metastases are confirmed: zoledronic acid 4 mg every 12 weeks after a dental examination, with calcium and vitamin D and calcium and creatinine checks before each dose; palliative radiation only if a lesion becomes painful or threatens fracture

Voice and work: injection medialization of the left vocal fold, voice therapy with a speech-language pathologist, infusions scheduled on his day off, and a graded return to rehearsal and performance as he chooses
Tobacco: confirm abstinence at each visit; no cessation treatment needed; record the smoking history for his care team
Tissue diagnosis, full staging, PD-L1, and comprehensive biomarker results before any systemic therapy, within three weeks of presentation
Diagnosis and stage by two weeks; PD-L1 at two weeks and tissue sequencing at three weeks; pembrolizumab started the day the sequencing was reviewed
First palliative care visit within eight weeks of diagnosis
Seen by the palliative care team two weeks after diagnosis
A voice strong enough for rehearsal by the second cycle
Louder, less breathy voice one week after injection medialization; light rehearsal resumed with voice therapy
No grade 2 or higher immune-related adverse event missed: laboratory panel before each infusion and symptom review at each visit
Panels normal before cycles 1 and 2; no symptoms of colitis, pneumonitis, hepatitis, or endocrine dysfunction
Zoledronic acid started only after a dental examination and normal calcium and kidney function
Dental examination three weeks earlier; calcium 9.4 and eGFR 92; first dose with cycle 2
